This trail reads Einstein's equations in the completed algebra, where gravity is a pair of gauge fields $\hb$ and $\Omega$ on flat spacetime. [[c:interior.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations]] Wherever $\hb$ is invertible, the vacuum equations become the constancy of one vector, the scale tractor. [[c:interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations]]

The equations themselves can be traced to horizons: under the local horizon premise and the Clausius relation, Jacobson's argument gives them, with $\Lambda$ an integration constant. [[c:synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius]] The temperature that argument needs follows from a premise with no temperature in it, the null ground state. [[c:synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises]] Its local form is now a theorem for every Hadamard state of the Dirac field. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise]]

Two things stay open. [[t]] The strength of gravity is still an input, matched only by choosing a cut-off. [[c:synthesis.series-content-induces-a-newton-coupling-only-through-an-unfixed-cut-off]] The ground-state clause still needs a time-independence that local conditions do not supply. [[c:synthesis.normality-on-the-closed-generator-gives-the-vacuum-folium-not-the-ground-state]]

The walk has three parts. [[t]] It first sets up the dictionary with Einstein's theory and follows two routes to his equations, with what each still assumes. [[t]] It then follows the quantum state on the horizon, which supplies the temperature, and ends by asking where that state could come from. [[t]]

title: What we assume

(C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$): on every local Rindler horizon the entropy of a cut is the integral of a curvature-independent area density (Loc) and, before matter crosses, the modes on the light rays are jointly thermal for the local boost (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$)
text: The series computes a temperature and an entropy for the edges of black holes and of the universe's horizon, using quantum modes it places on those edges. Jacobson showed in 1995 that Einstein's equations of gravity follow if every small piece of horizon around every point, including the horizon seen by an accelerating observer, has a temperature set by the acceleration and an entropy proportional to its area, by the same amount everywhere. This assumption says exactly that, with the quantum modes running continuously along the light rays of each small horizon and being the same field as the matter that falls through it. It has two parts: the entropy of a slice of the horizon is its area times a fixed number that does not depend on how strong the gravitational field is there, and before matter falls through, the modes are thermal at the accelerating observer's temperature. Where there is no gravitational field the second part now follows from a simpler assumption with no temperature in it; the first part is still assumed. With it, the store proves Einstein's equations, with the strength of gravity set by the entropy per area and the cosmological constant left free. The assumption would fail if the entropy per area turned out to depend on the strength of the gravitational field or on matter, or if gravity were found to deviate from Einstein's equations.

title: (FS), the field-space premise of the gravitational action: the varied gravitational connection, a $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field with nondegenerate soldering, admits a parallel tractor $I$ with $\ip{X}{I} = 1$ (the physical scale), a holonomy reduction to the stabiliser of $I$
text: The series borrows a rule, an action, from which the equations of gravity follow, and that rule gives Einstein's equations only if one decides in advance which shapes of the gravitational field are allowed to vary: those that keep one special fixed direction, the frozen point, unchanged everywhere, measured in the actual scale of the spacetime. Without that decision the same rule gives a different theory, conformal gravity. Several attempts to derive the decision from the series' own structures failed; each turned out to be the same assumption in another form. So it is recorded as an assumption of its own. It explains why the cosmological constant is a fixed number, but for the same reason a measurement that dark energy never changes would not count as separate evidence for it. It would be refuted if dark energy were found to change, or if gravity were found to deviate from Einstein's equations where the rule applies.

title: (HD), the Hadamard deposit premise: the descent's deposited state is a Hadamard state on a Cauchy collar of the descent, for the Dirac field and for the scalar fields of the descended phase; the occupation profile over an admissible reference vacuum stays free data
text: Quantum fields in a gravitational field make sense only in well-behaved states, called Hadamard states, which look like empty space at very short distances. The series' account of the universe's earliest moment, the descent, leaves its fields in some state, but nothing in the series yet shows that state is well behaved. This premise assumes it: just after the descent the state is of the well-behaved kind. Since good behaviour, once present, is kept by the equations of motion, every later situation, including black holes formed by collapse, then has well-behaved states, which is what the series' horizon results and the energy of quantum fields need. The premise does not say which well-behaved state it is, how many particles of each energy were left behind, or what pattern of primordial ripples they carry; those remain open inputs.

title: (N$_{+}$): on the continuum of a horizon's null generators the state of the modes is a gauge-invariant quasi-free ground state for the affine null translations along the generators
text: Black holes, the horizon of an expanding universe and the horizon an accelerating observer sees all have a temperature. The series used to assume each temperature with its own premise. This premise replaces them with one assumption that mentions no temperature: the quantum modes running along each horizon's light rays are in their lowest-energy state for sliding along the rays. The store proves that this state, seen from one side of the horizon, is exactly thermal at the expected temperature. The assumption describes a black hole that has always existed in equilibrium; read on the light rays falling into the horizon, its short-distance form also covers a hole formed by collapse, given a simplification of the radiating fields to one direction per light ray. For the horizon an accelerating observer sees, and for the cosmological horizon with fields that keep their form under rescalings of lengths, it amounts to choosing the standard vacuum of the field theory. It still carries an input: that the state is smooth where the two halves of the horizon meet, the condition every derivation of black-hole temperature uses in some form. A black hole that has always existed in equilibrium is an idealisation in a universe with a positive cosmological constant, where no such equilibrium state exists, so the local form of the assumption is the one that matters there; whether the series' states are smooth enough at short distances to give that local form everywhere is still open, though it now comes down to the usual short-distance requirement on states: how such states look at very short distances where gravity is present, assumed before, is now proved.

title: Einstein's equations in the completion

text: Each step in this part either translates Einstein's theory into the completed algebra or asks where its equations come from. [[t]]

We start from the bridge between the two languages. [[t]]

Gauge Theory Gravity describes gravity by two gauge fields on flat spacetime, $\hb$ and $\Omega$. [[c:interior.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations]] Wherever $\hb$ is invertible its field equations are equivalent to Einstein's for the derived metric \[ g(a,b) = \hb^{-1}(a)\cdot\hb^{-1}(b) \] and in vacuum to that metric being Ricci-flat. [[c:interior.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations]]

title: Imported: equivalence with the Einstein equations
text: Gauge theory gravity rewrites general relativity in the language of geometric algebra. This imported result says that, wherever its basic field can be inverted, its equations say exactly the same as Einstein's equations for the corresponding metric. In empty space this means the metric has vanishing Ricci curvature.
provenance: A. Lasenby, C. Doran and S. Gull, Gravity, gauge theories and geometric algebra, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. A 356 (1998), 487--582., \S 4 (\S 4.3, covariant forms of the field equations), App.~C; C. Doran and A. Lasenby, Geometric Algebra for Physicists, Cambridge University Press (2003)., Ch.~13-14

text:
To read those equations in the completion we use the tractor bundle: the vectors $\sigma\nInf + \mu + \rho\nO$ of $\Cl(2,4)$, with a natural connection built from the Schouten tensor $\Sch$, a rearranged form of the curvature. [[c:interior.imported-tractor-connection]]

This step records two facts: the connection preserves the square $Q$ of $\Cl(2,4)$, and a Schouten map proportional to the identity forces \[ c = \tfrac{R}{24} \] [[c:interior.metric-parallelism-trace-schouten-condition]] In particular $\Sch = 0$ exactly when $\Ric = 0$. [[c:interior.metric-parallelism-trace-schouten-condition]]

title: Metric parallelism, and the trace of the Schouten condition
text: This lemma records two elementary facts behind the tractor form of the gravitational field equations. First, the natural derivative on the tractor bundle, which on flat spacetime is a field of rotations of the six-dimensional conformal model, respects that model's own notion of length. Second, if the Schouten tensor, a rearranged form of the gravitational field strength, is a multiple of the metric then the field is Einstein, and the Schouten tensor vanishes exactly when the Ricci curvature does.

With those two facts the vacuum equations can be repackaged. [[t]]

Carrying the null scale tractor $
Inf$ along with the tractor gauge field gives \[ D^{T}_{a}
Inf = -\Sch igl(\hb^{-1}(a) igr) \] [[c:interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations]] So $
Inf$ is parallel exactly when $\Sch = 0$, that is, exactly when the derived metric is Ricci-flat. [[c:interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations]]

title: Covariant form of the vacuum equations
text: In the interior region, Einstein's equations for empty space can be recast as a single condition on the gravitational fields: a particular marker in the six-dimensional conformal extension of spacetime, attached to the physical scale, must stay constant as it is carried from point to point by a gauge field built from gravity. This result proves that the two formulations are exactly equivalent, and that the marker is a null (lightlike) object. It also notes that merely having some constant marker of this kind is a weaker condition that does not by itself give the field equations.

The same rewriting works when a cosmological constant is present. [[c:interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone]]

For an Einstein metric with constant $\Lambda$ the parallel section is \[ I_g = \nInf + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\,\nO \] with squared norm $Q(I_g) = \Lambda/3$. [[c:interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone]] It is null only when $\Lambda = 0$; any nonzero constant moves it off the cone. [[c:interior.scale-tractor-leaves-cone]]

title: $\Lambda \neq 0$: the scale tractor leaves the cone
text: Einstein's equations with a cosmological constant can be written as the statement that one vector of the six-dimensional conformal model, the scale tractor, is unchanged as the gravitational gauge fields carry it from point to point. Its squared length turns out to be the cosmological constant divided by three. With no cosmological constant it has zero length, and any nonzero cosmological constant moves it off the cone of zero-length directions.

All of this rewriting would be suspect if it changed the physics, and this step says it does not. [[t]]

Where the gauge field is invertible and $\Lambda = 0$, the series' description is not an approximation to general relativity but the same theory, its vacuum equations being the parallelism of the scale tractor. [[c:hawking.imported-exterior-exactly-general-relativity]]

title: Imported: the exterior is exactly general relativity
text: Away from the places where the series' new structure matters, its description of gravity is not an approximation to general relativity but the same theory. With no cosmological constant, both the field equations and their geometric repackaging agree exactly with Einstein's theory in that region.

So far the equations were taken from Einstein. [[t]] The series also asks why they hold, and its first answer runs through horizons. [[t]]

The local horizon premise (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) speaks about every local Rindler horizon, the small horizon an accelerating observer sees near any point. [[c:synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise]] Its first clause, (Loc), says the entropy of a cut is $\int \eta\, dA$ with a density $\eta$ that depends neither on the field strength nor on matter, and horizon entropy carries no Euler term. [[c:synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise]] Its second clause, (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), says that before matter crosses, the modes on the light rays are thermal for the local boost at rapidity period $2\pi$, which is the temperature $a/2\pi$. [[c:synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise]] It is adopted as a premise, and (Loc) is not derived on either reading of the entropy. [[c:synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise]]

Add the Clausius relation, that heat crossing the patch raises its entropy by heat over temperature, and Jacobson's 1995 argument goes through. [[c:synthesis.imported-jacobson-clausius-1995]] The store writes it out with every hypothesis named and obtains \[ \mathcal{R}(a) + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,T(a) = (\Lambda + 4\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,\tau)\,a, \qquad G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 1/(4\eta) \] with $\Lambda$ an integration constant. [[c:synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius]] What picks out Einstein's equations over more complicated ones is that $\eta$ ignores the curvature. [[c:synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius]] The route also takes the whole stress as its source, through the null components $T(k,k)$ in every null direction. [[c:synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius]]

title: Under (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and the Clausius relation, Jacobson's argument gives Einstein's equations with $\Lambda$ an integration constant and $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 1/(4\eta)$; every further hypothesis named
text: In 1995 Ted Jacobson showed that Einstein's equations of gravity follow if every small patch of horizon, as seen by an accelerating observer, has a temperature set by the acceleration and an entropy proportional to its area, and if heat crossing the patch raises its entropy by heat divided by temperature. The series assumes, as a premise, that its own horizon quantum modes give that temperature and that entropy on all such small horizons. This result writes the argument out step by step under that premise and checks each algebraic step exactly. It also lists everything else the argument needs: that the heat is the energy carried by matter and nothing else changes the entropy, that the horizon patch is momentarily neither expanding nor shearing, that matter is described by an ordinary conserved energy tensor, that the gravitational field is smooth enough, and that space-time has four dimensions. Given all that, Einstein's equations follow, with the strength of gravity fixed by the entropy per area and the cosmological constant left free. What singles out Einstein's equations, rather than more complicated versions of them, is that the entropy per area is the same everywhere and does not depend on the strength of the gravitational field there. The derivation is conditional: it shows what the premise would deliver, not that the premise holds.

The series has a second route to the same equations, through an action. [[t]]

The borrowed MacDowell-Mansouri functional gives Einstein's equations only if the varied connection admits a parallel tractor $I$ with $\ip{X}{I} = 1$, the frozen point, so that $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ is constant. [[c:synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point]] Without that restriction the same integrand is the Weyl square, which gives conformal gravity instead. [[c:synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point]] No route derives the restriction from transport, so it is adopted as a premise of its own, the field-space premise (FS), refuted by a confirmed $w \neq -1$. [[c:synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point]]

Kept side by side, the two routes constrain each other. [[t]] With the action's single coupling $G$ and $\Lambda \neq 0$, the Clausius relation at rapidity period $2\pi c$ holds where matter crosses exactly when $\eta = c/(4G)$. [[c:synthesis.clausius-on-the-action-shell-ties-entropy-density-to-period]] So, given the calibration $\eta = \tfrac14$ at the action's $G$, the one coupling of (Loc) and the period of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) imply each other there, and the Clausius relation becomes a constraint on the thermal data rather than a derivation. [[c:synthesis.clausius-on-the-action-shell-ties-entropy-density-to-period]] In empty regions it says nothing. [[c:synthesis.clausius-on-the-action-shell-ties-entropy-density-to-period]]

title: If the field equations are those of the field-space action with one normalisation $G$ and $\Lambda \neq 0$, and the Clausius relation holds on local patches at rapidity period $2\pi c$, then at every point where the stress is not a multiple of the metric the Clausius relation is exactly $\eta = c/(4G)$ (Jacobson's identification at period $2\pi c$); so, given the calibration $\eta = \tfrac14$ with the action's $G$ in the same units ($G = 1$), the one-coupling clause of (Loc) and the period of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) imply each other where matter crosses and the stored independence model of each fails there given the other datum, while on matter-free regions the relation is empty
text: The series has two ways of getting Einstein's equations for gravity. One borrows a standard action principle with a single strength of gravity. The other uses horizon thermodynamics: entropy proportional to area, a temperature set by acceleration, and heat flowing in as energy crosses a horizon. On the thermodynamic route alone, two ingredients were known to be independent assumptions: that the entropy per unit area does not depend on what matter is present, and the exact temperature of small horizons. This result asks what happens when both routes are kept, as the series now does. Wherever matter crosses a horizon, the heat balance then becomes a single equation tying the entropy per area to the temperature factor and the strength of gravity. Once the entropy per area is fixed at its standard value in the same units as the strength of gravity, either assumption gives the other there, and the known counterexamples stop working. The core equation is Jacobson's 1995 link between horizon entropy and the strength of gravity. In empty regions the equation says nothing, and the temperature remains a separate assumption there.

Both routes are stated for every gravitational field, so it matters which fields the series' quantum structure can reach. [[t]] That turns on the tidal part of the curvature. [[t]]

In four dimensions the tidal (Weyl) part of the curvature splits into two duality halves, the eigenspaces of multiplication by the unit pseudoscalar. [[c:correspondence.no-real-lorentzian-vacuum-half-flat]] For a real gravitational field the halves are conjugate, so if one vanishes so does the other, and the derived metric is conformally flat. [[c:correspondence.no-real-lorentzian-vacuum-half-flat]] Real black holes such as Schwarzschild and Kerr are therefore never half-flat. [[c:correspondence.no-real-lorentzian-vacuum-half-flat]]

title: No real Lorentzian vacuum is half-flat
text: In four dimensions the part of the gravitational field strength that describes tidal forces splits into two mirror-image halves. For a real gravitational field with one time direction the two halves are complex conjugates, so if one vanishes so does the other, and the geometry the field describes is then flat up to a change of scale. Real black holes such as Schwarzschild and Kerr are therefore never half-flat, which is why Penrose's construction of such spaces from spinor geometry (the nonlinear graviton) is stated only in complex or Euclidean settings.

The series attaches its quantum particles to spacetime through twistors, and twistor transport is path independent exactly where the Weyl curvature vanishes. [[c:synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nordstrom-not-einstein]] On those fields Einstein's equations allow only perfect fluids of uniform rest density and constant-curvature vacuum, while Nordstr\"om's trace equation can be solved for any matter. [[c:synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nordstrom-not-einstein]]

So consistency on the fields where the twistors attach does not single out Einstein's equations. [[c:synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nordstrom-not-einstein]] Nordstr\"om's theory, ruled out by observation because it deflects no light, passes every consistency check there. [[c:synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nordstrom-not-einstein]]

title: On the gravitational fields where twistor transport is path independent, exactly those with vanishing Weyl curvature, Einstein's equations admit no perfect fluid whose density varies on its rest spaces and no vacuum field but constant curvature, while Nordstr\"om's trace equation is solvable for every stress trace with no condition on the matter; so the consistency conditions of a coupled system on these fields (Bianchi identities, conservation, second order, the Newtonian limit) do not give Einstein's equations without the clause that the whole stress map is the source
text: The series attaches its quantum particles to spacetime through twistors, a space that is the same at every point only where the gravitational field has no tidal part of a particular kind (the Weyl curvature, the part that bends light around a star and travels as gravitational waves). Such fields are rescalings of flat spacetime. If Einstein's equations hold on them, the matter they contain must be spread evenly in its own rest frame: a star or a lumpy dust cloud cannot sit in such a field, and empty space can curve only uniformly, so the space outside a body is not of this kind. On the same fields an older theory of gravity, Nordstr\"om's, in which only the trace of the matter's stress-energy sources gravity, works for any matter at all, satisfies every consistency requirement, and reproduces Newton's law. It is ruled out by observation (it bends no light, and it gives the wrong advance of Mercury's perihelion, minus one sixth of Einstein's), so it is a counterexample to the logic, not a viable theory. So requiring the coupled system of matter and gravity to be consistent on the fields where the twistors attach does not single out Einstein's equations; something more is needed: the rule that the whole stress-energy, not only its trace, is the source, or an attachment of the particles that works where the Weyl curvature is nonzero.

What Nordstr\"om's theory lacks is Einstein's rule that the whole stress, not only its trace, is the source. [[c:synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nordstrom-not-einstein]] This step asks whether a symmetry supplies that rule. [[t]]

At first order, at each non-null momentum, there are exactly four classes of gravitational fields closed under displacements. [[c:synthesis.weyl-flat-variations-carry-only-the-stress-trace-and-the-whole-stress-clause-is-the-trace-free-channel]] Varying only within the Weyl-flat class, the attachment's domain, couples gravity to the stress trace alone and decouples the Maxwell field, so gauge invariance does not give the rule. [[c:synthesis.weyl-flat-variations-carry-only-the-stress-trace-and-the-whole-stress-clause-is-the-trace-free-channel]] The missing part is the trace-free channel, exactly what the null fluxes $k \cdot T(k)$ of the Clausius route see. [[c:synthesis.weyl-flat-variations-carry-only-the-stress-trace-and-the-whole-stress-clause-is-the-trace-free-channel]] Under an action principle the rule amounts to varying the field off the attachment's domain. [[c:synthesis.weyl-flat-variations-carry-only-the-stress-trace-and-the-whole-stress-clause-is-the-trace-free-channel]]

title: At first order, at each non-null momentum, the classes of gravitational fields that are closed under displacements and covariant under the stabiliser of the momentum are exactly four (at null momentum there are further classes, among them gauge plus the two helicity-two directions); varying the field only within the Weyl-flat class, the domain of the twistor attachment, couples it to the stress trace alone, and the Maxwell field not at all, so displacement gauge invariance does not give the whole-stress clause; the clause is the trace-free channel, which the null fluxes see exactly and which with conservation fixes a conserved source at every nonzero momentum
text: Einstein's theory says that everything about matter's energy, momentum and pressure is a source of the gravitational field. An older rival, Nordstr\"om's, used only one number made from them, their trace, and is ruled out because it does not deflect light. The series wants to derive Einstein's rule from its own field theory. This result shows what that requires. If gravity's field is only allowed to change in the ways that keep the derived metric a rescaling of the flat one, which are exactly the fields where the series' twistors can be attached, then it responds only to the trace, as in Nordstr\"om's theory, and light and other massless fields do not affect it at all, even though this restricted theory respects every change of coordinates. The full rule needs the field to be able to change in five further ways that leave those fields. (For waves moving at the speed of light the bookkeeping has a few more cases, but the conclusion is the same.) The light-ray form of Einstein's equations used elsewhere in the series sees exactly the part that the trace misses, and energy conservation then fills in the rest, up to a cosmological constant. So the missing step is not a symmetry; it is that the matter theory must work, and be varied, beyond the fields where the twistors attach.

The last question on this side is the strength of gravity itself. [[t]]

In Sakharov's induced gravity the series' content produces $1/G$ from its quantum fluctuations; with a proper-time cut-off $\Lambda$, here a cut-off and not the cosmological constant, \[ 1/G = \bigl[B\Lambda^{2} - \textstyle\sum w\, m^{2}\ln(\Lambda^{2}/m^{2})\bigr]/(12\pi) \] [[c:synthesis.series-content-induces-a-newton-coupling-only-through-an-unfixed-cut-off]] If only the weak-scale content lies below the cut-off, the count $B$ vanishes and the remainder has the wrong sign and is far too small. [[c:synthesis.series-content-induces-a-newton-coupling-only-through-an-unfixed-cut-off]] Where $B > 0$ the observed $G$ can be matched, but only by choosing the cut-off to match it, which is a fit. [[c:synthesis.series-content-induces-a-newton-coupling-only-through-an-unfixed-cut-off]] On this route $G$ stays an input. [[c:synthesis.series-content-induces-a-newton-coupling-only-through-an-unfixed-cut-off]]

title: In the Feynman gauge with a proper-time cut-off $\Lambda$ the series' content induces $1/G = [B\Lambda^{2} - \sum w m^{2}\ln(\Lambda^{2}/m^{2})]/(12\pi) + O(m^{2})$, with $B = -36$ plus the scalars' weights for the chain's Pati-Salam content under Hypothesis (S); the logarithmic remainder is repulsive if the content below $\Lambda$ is the weak-scale content alone with $B = 0$, its sign is not fixed by the store for a cut-off above $M_{I}$ under (S), and it stays far below $1/G$; where $B > 0$ matching $G$ fixes $\Lambda$, so the route gives $G$ only by choosing the cut-off
text: Sakharov's idea is that gravity's strength could be produced by the quantum jitter of all other fields, up to some shortest length where the jitter is cut off. The result is the cut-off energy squared times a count of the fields, plus a much smaller term from the particle masses. If the series' larger unified symmetry is real at high energies, the count depends on how its many extra Higgs fields couple to curvature, which nothing in the series decides. If only the everyday particles lie below the cut-off and their count is zero, the small mass term is left, and it has the wrong sign: it would make gravity repulsive, and it is far too weak. With the series' unified symmetry, heavy force carriers pull the other way and the sign is undecided, but the term is still far too weak. Where the count is positive, gravity's observed strength can be matched, but only by choosing the cut-off to match it, a little above the Planck energy. The series has no number that would set that cut-off, so on this route the strength of gravity remains an input.

title: Temperature and Hawking radiation

text: This part follows the temperature that the horizon route needs back to a statement about the quantum state, and asks how much of that statement is now proved. [[t]]

The temperature clause can be traded for a premise of a different kind. [[t]] Premise (N$_{+}$) says only that the modes on a horizon's light rays are in a ground state for sliding along the rays, with no temperature in it. [[c:synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state]]

Seen from one side of the edge, that ground state is exactly thermal at rapidity period $2\pi$: the period comes out of positive energy and of the observer seeing only half of each ray. [[c:synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises]] So the continuum forms of (R) for the eternal hole, of (R$_{\Lambda}$) and of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) in Minkowski space all follow from one premise. [[c:synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises]] The input that remains is regularity across the bifurcation surface, where the horizon's two halves meet. [[c:synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises]]

title: A ground state for the affine null translations of a horizon's generators restricts on either side of the edge to the continuum I-state at rapidity period $2\pi$, so the continuum restatements of (R) for the eternal hole, (R$_{\Lambda}$), (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and the joint KMS part of (Q) follow from one premise with no temperature in it, posable only on the continuum
text: Black holes, the horizon of an expanding universe, and the small horizons an accelerating observer sees all have a temperature. The series has so far assumed each of these temperatures with a separate premise of the same kind, each fixing a period of $2\pi$ by hand. This result shows that a single assumption with no temperature in it gives all three, once the quantum modes are taken to run continuously along each horizon's light rays. The assumption is that these modes are in their lowest-energy state with respect to sliding along the rays. Looked at from one side of the horizon, that state is exactly thermal, and the $2\pi$ comes out of the calculation, because energy is positive and the observer sees only half of each ray. There are costs. The finite lists of modes the series counts become an approximation. For a black hole the assumption describes an eternal hole in equilibrium, not one formed by collapse. And the assumption is still an input: it says the state is smooth across the point where the horizon's two halves meet, which is what every derivation of black-hole temperature assumes in some form.

Where gravity is present, what the horizon route uses is a local form of (N$_{+}$), at each point of each local horizon. [[c:synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state]]

On a single generator, the light-ray version of the Hadamard condition holds exactly when the state differs from the null vacuum by a smooth kernel. [[c:synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state]] With no stationarity and no temperature, that gives the local form of (N$_{+}$) at every point. [[c:synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state]] It does not single out the vacuum, since thermal states pass it too. [[c:synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state]]

title: On a horizon generator the generator analogue of the microlocal (Hadamard) condition, on both orderings of the two-point kernel, is equivalent to a smooth difference from the null vacuum, so with no stationarity and no temperature it gives the local form of (N$_{+}$) at every point (with the stored theorem and boost stationarity at the edge, (N$_{+}$)); the affine-KMS states satisfy it, so it does not select the ground state
text: Physicists usually require that any reasonable quantum state, looked at closely enough, resembles empty space. The precise version of this requirement says that the very fine-grained structure of the state carries only positive energy. This result writes a version of that requirement for the quantum modes running along a single light ray of a horizon and shows that it is the same as saying the state differs from the vacuum only by something smooth. From there the store's earlier results give the horizon temperature at every point, without assuming that anything is static. It does not single out the vacuum, though: a gas of modes at any temperature also passes, so to get the full premise one still needs the state to be static near the point where the two halves of the horizon meet. Whether the series' states obey the requirement is still an open assumption.

The question becomes whether physically reasonable states satisfy that condition on the light rays. [[t]] Where there is no gravitational field, the answer is yes. [[t]]

On the flat field every gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state of the Dirac field restricts on every null plane to the generator condition. [[c:synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes]] So the local form of (N$_{+}$) holds at every point of every local Rindler horizon there. [[c:synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes]]

title: On the flat gravitational field every gauge-invariant quasi-free Dirac state differing from a vacuum by a smooth kernel restricts on every null plane to a state satisfying the generator microlocal condition, the vacuum itself to the null vacuum, so it has the local form of (N$_{+}$) on every local Rindler horizon; not the ground-state clause, not nonzero field strength
text: The series' account of horizon temperature rests on an assumption that, very close to any point of a horizon, the quantum field looks like empty space. This result checks that assumption against the field theory in empty flat space. On any light-like plane, the field's vacuum, whatever the particle's mass, looks exactly like the empty state that the assumption names, and every state that physicists regard as reasonable, one that differs from the vacuum only smoothly, looks like it at short distances too. So in flat space the assumption's short-distance part is a consequence of the field theory, though not the part that says the state is the vacuum everywhere, and not yet in a gravitational field.

With gravity present the work splits into two parts, the bulk and the light rays. [[t]]

In the bulk, a gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state of the Dirac field of any mass, looked at closely enough at any point of a globally hyperbolic gravitational field, becomes the flat massless vacuum. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-dirac-states-scale-to-the-flat-massless-vacuum-at-every-point-of-a-gravitational-field]] This is a standard theorem of Sahlmann and Verch, redone in the spacetime algebra: the mass, the connection and the curvature fade out of the correlations at definite rates. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-dirac-states-scale-to-the-flat-massless-vacuum-at-every-point-of-a-gravitational-field]]

title: Given the Hadamard parametrix of the squared Dirac operator (imported), every gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state of the Dirac field of mass m0 >= 0 on a globally hyperbolic gravitational field scales, under the store's dilation in a gauge with hb(x0) = 1, to the flat field's massless vacuum on both orderings (standard: Sahlmann and Verch 2001, Prop. 5.6, re-derived in the spacetime algebra for Dirac spinors), so clause (a) of (HS) holds and the premise's content is its generator clause (b)
text: The series assumed that any state of the free electron field of the standard regular kind (gauge-invariant, quasi-free and Hadamard), looked at closely enough at a point where gravity is present, resembles the empty state of flat space. This result proves that assumption for the bulk of space-time, for massive and massless particles and for every gravitational field with a well-posed causal structure (globally hyperbolic), by redoing in the series' algebra a known theorem of Sahlmann and Verch from the mathematical physics literature: close up, the curvature, the mass and the gravitational connection all fade out of the state's correlations at definite rates. It relies on two standard analytic facts quoted from the literature rather than proved in the series. What it does not prove is the companion statement the series also needs: that the same is true when the state is looked at only along the light rays of a small horizon. That part stays an assumption.

On the light rays the danger is that gravity's tidal stretching of the rays leaves a mark at the shortest distances. [[t]]

At leading order it does not: on a null hypersurface the Weyl and Ricci field strength along the generators, the expansion and the shear cancel exactly from the leading singularity, because \[ \Delta^{1/2}/\sqrt{\det M} = (a(u)\,a(u'))^{-1/2} \] [[c:synthesis.field-strength-cancels-from-the-leading-null-singularity-of-hadamard-dirac-states-on-null-hypersurfaces]] Hadamard states differ there by smooth kernels, so the question no longer depends on the state, only on the geometry. [[c:synthesis.field-strength-cancels-from-the-leading-null-singularity-of-hadamard-dirac-states-on-null-hypersurfaces]]

title: On every null hypersurface of a gravitational field generated by affine null geodesics, the field strength along the generators, the expansion and the shear cancel exactly from the coefficient of the leading null singularity of a Hadamard Dirac kernel restricted to it, which at leading order in the canonical normalisation is the null vacuum; restricted kernels of Hadamard states differ by smooth kernels, so clause (b) of (HS) is a property of the field and reduces to a remainder bound on the Hadamard parametrix, argued but not proved
text: The series assumes that, looked at closely along the light rays that make up a small horizon, any reasonable quantum state of the electron field resembles empty space, even where gravity is present. One way this could fail is if gravity's tidal stretching of the light rays left a mark on the state at the shortest distances. This result shows that, at the leading order, it does not: the tidal effects change how light rays spread and how distances between them are measured, but the two changes cancel exactly. It also shows that the assumption is either true for all reasonable states or for none, so it is really a question about gravity's geometry, not about which state the world is in. Smaller correction terms needed a technical estimate, argued here and proved by a later result.

Two smaller corrections could each have grown without limit. [[t]]

They cancel: on every local Rindler horizon, for every mass, the restricted Dirac Hadamard parametrix is the null vacuum $W_{0}\otimes\id_{K}$ plus a bounded kernel, the $\log\epsilon$ terms cancelling identically. [[c:synthesis.restricted-dirac-hadamard-parametrix-on-a-null-hypersurface-is-the-null-vacuum-plus-a-bounded-kernel]] So the remainder has generator scaling degree at most $0$. [[c:synthesis.restricted-dirac-hadamard-parametrix-on-a-null-hypersurface-is-the-null-vacuum-plus-a-bounded-kernel]]

title: On every piece of a geodesic null hypersurface of a gravitational field whose distinct generators are spacelike separated (every small enough piece, every local Rindler horizon), the Dirac Hadamard parametrix, restricted to the generators in the canonical normalisation as the epsilon-regularised transverse-smeared limit, is the null vacuum plus a bounded kernel: the log epsilon terms cancel identically, so the remainder bound posed by (HS) holds for every mass
text: The series needs every reasonable quantum state of the electron field to look like empty space along the light rays of the small horizons used to derive the equations of gravity, when looked at closely enough. The question had been reduced to a statement about gravity's geometry alone: a fixed mathematical object, which carries the short-distance behaviour shared by all reasonable states, should look like that of empty space along those light rays, up to corrections that fade at short distances. The strongest part had been checked before; two weaker pieces, which separately would grow without limit, were expected but not shown to cancel. This result shows that they do cancel exactly, on small enough pieces of the light sheets of every gravitational field (including the small horizons the series uses) and for every mass of the field, and that everything left over stays bounded. So the assumed statement is now proved, for the precise way the object is restricted to the light rays. One step remains before it applies to the states themselves: showing that this way of restricting agrees with the more fundamental one.

That computation used one particular way of restricting to the light rays, so the restriction itself has to be put on firm ground. [[t]]

The Dirac current is future causal, so the flux through a null sheet never exceeds the total: $W^{+} + W^{-} = \iota_{\mathcal{H}}^{*}\iota_{\mathcal{H}} \le 1$. [[c:synthesis.dirac-states-restrict-to-null-hypersurfaces-through-the-flux-contraction-and-are-thin-layer-limits-under-the-generator-car]] Hence every state of the Dirac field restricts to the generators with no characteristic Cauchy problem, and Hadamard states differ there by smooth kernels. [[c:synthesis.dirac-states-restrict-to-null-hypersurfaces-through-the-flux-contraction-and-are-thin-layer-limits-under-the-generator-car]] If the anticommutation relations hold on the generators, the restriction is the limit of the bulk two-point function on thinner and thinner layers. [[c:synthesis.dirac-states-restrict-to-null-hypersurfaces-through-the-flux-contraction-and-are-thin-layer-limits-under-the-generator-car]]

title: Every state of the Dirac field on a gravitational field restricts to a null hypersurface through the flux contraction of the conserved current, with no characteristic Cauchy problem, its restricted kernels have generator scaling degree at most one, and restricted kernels of Hadamard states differ by smooth pullbacks; if the generator anticommutation relations hold on nearby null hypersurfaces (proved in the literature for light cones), the restriction is the thin-layer limit of the bulk two-point function, and the restricted Hadamard parametrix then has a regularisation-free definition, whose agreement with the regularised one used in (HS) is argued
text: The series assumes that, seen closely along the light rays of a small horizon, quantum states of the electron field look like empty space. Testing this needs a precise way to look at a state "on the light rays only", and the earlier work borrowed one from memory. This result builds it from a basic fact: the flow of electron charge-current is never faster than light, so what flows through a sheet of light rays can never exceed the total. That alone makes every state restrict to the light rays, caps how singular the restriction can be, and shows that any two reasonable states differ there only by a smooth amount. If the light-ray field also obeys the usual rules for fermions, which mathematicians have proved for light cones but which are only believed for general light sheets, then the restriction is simply the limit of ordinary measurements made in thinner and thinner slabs, and the earlier borrowed step is no longer needed. Whether this matches the way the horizon assumption itself is computed is argued, not proved.

Those anticommutation relations were the remaining condition. [[t]]

On every geodesic null hypersurface the Dirac causal propagator between the sheet and a nearby leaf tends to the canonical delta kernel on the generators, the one possible correction vanishing by the same half-density law. [[c:synthesis.dirac-causal-propagator-between-nearby-null-leaves-tends-to-the-generator-car-on-every-geodesic-null-hypersurface]] So the generator anticommutation relations hold, local Rindler horizons included. [[c:synthesis.dirac-causal-propagator-between-nearby-null-leaves-tends-to-the-generator-car-on-every-geodesic-null-hypersurface]]

title: On every geodesic null hypersurface of a gravitational field the causal propagator of the Dirac field, restricted between the hypersurface and a nearby leaf of a null foliation, tends to the canonical delta kernel of the generators, the step term cancelling by the half-density law; with the flux contraction of the conserved current, the generator anticommutation relations hold there, and the restricted Hadamard parametrix in the thin-layer definition is the null vacuum plus a bounded kernel
text: Earlier work needed a basic rule for the electron field seen only along the light rays of a small horizon: the field there should obey the standard rules for fermions, exactly as in empty space. Mathematicians had proved this for light cones; for the general light sheets used in the series it was only believed. This result proves it for every such sheet by a short calculation with the one object every state shares, the propagator that carries signals at or below light speed. Two corrections that could have spoiled the rule turn out to cancel, because the area of the sheet and the focusing of light rays are tied together. Together with two companion results, it also shows that every reasonable state looks like empty space along these light rays at short distances.

The pieces now assemble into one theorem. [[t]]

(HS), formerly a premise, is proved: for every gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state of the Dirac field of any mass, at every point of every local Rindler horizon of every gravitational field, the scaling limit on the generators is the null vacuum. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise]] That is the local form of (N$_{+}$) at every such point. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise]] It rests on imported standard results and on a few standard inputs cited from memory, such as a local null foliation and the Morse lemma with parameters, and it is stated for the free Dirac field only. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise]] It does not give the ground-state clause of (N$_{+}$), nor (Loc), nor which state the world is in. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise]]

title: (HS), the Hadamard scaling limit, a theorem (formerly a premise): for every gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state of the Dirac field of any mass on a gravitational field, at every point of every local Rindler horizon, the bulk scaling limit is the flat massless vacuum and the restriction to the generators through the flux trace has the null vacuum as its generator scaling limit, the epsilon-regularised restriction of the parametrix agreeing with it modulo a bounded time-function-dependent kernel; hence the local form of (N$_{+}$) at every such point for these states
text: Physicists require that any reasonable quantum state, looked at closely enough, resembles empty space. The series had assumed this along the light rays of the small horizons used to derive the equations of gravity, wherever gravity is present. It is now proved, for the electron field of any mass, given standard results from the literature: the flow of electric charge through a sheet of light can never exceed the total, signals travel at or below light speed, and two growing corrections cancel because the area of the sheet and the focusing of its light rays are tied together. So every reasonable state looks like empty space along those light rays at short distances, which is what the series' horizon temperature needs locally. It does not pick out which state the world is in, and it does not by itself give the full horizon assumption, since warm states pass the test too.

The ground-state clause is the part of the null ground-state premise that this leaves open. [[t]]

Asking the state to look like the null vacuum near every point of a generator, including the point at infinity where the vacuum's symmetries close the generator up, puts it in the null vacuum's family, its folium, with positive translations along the ray. [[c:synthesis.normality-on-the-closed-generator-gives-the-vacuum-folium-not-the-ground-state]] Being the null vacuum itself, which is (N$_{+}$), still needs translation or boost stationarity. [[c:synthesis.normality-on-the-closed-generator-gives-the-vacuum-folium-not-the-ground-state]] Normality at finite points alone does not even fix the family: a state with a kink at infinity passes it. [[c:synthesis.normality-on-the-closed-generator-gives-the-vacuum-folium-not-the-ground-state]]

title: On a horizon generator closed by its Moebius covariance, the Hilbert-Schmidt form of local normality to the null vacuum on every interval, the arcs through the point at infinity included, is a globally square-integrable two-point difference; for pure gauge-invariant quasi-free states this is global quasi-equivalence with the null vacuum, the folium form of (N$_{+}$) with the affine translations positive in the state's representation, and it gives (N$_{+}$) itself only with translation or boost stationarity; it excludes the affine-KMS states on one far end, while normality at every finite point, the vacuum on each far end separately and implementability of the affine group do not fix the folium
text: The series assumes that the quantum field on the light rays of a horizon is in its lowest-energy state. Earlier work showed that for a field that does not change in time this is the same as a standard locality requirement at the point where the horizon's light rays begin. Here the time-independence is dropped. Looking like the vacuum near every point of a light ray is not enough, since a warm state does so too; asking for the vacuum far along the ray rules out the warm state, but a subtler state still passes if the two far ends are tested separately. Joining the two ends of a light ray at one point, as the symmetries of the vacuum allow, and requiring the vacuum's local behaviour there as well puts the state in the vacuum's family, where energy along the ray is never negative; being the vacuum itself still needs time-independence.

title: Quantum fields in one algebra

text: The last part asks where the series' quantum state could come from. [[t]]

The natural candidate is the series' own attachment of quantum modes to spacetime through conformal spinors, which in flat space comes with a built-in positive energy. [[c:synthesis.attachment-transport-is-flat-only-where-weyl-vanishes]]

On a gravitational field those spinors can be parallel for the tractor gauge field only where the Weyl curvature vanishes: a two-dimensional subspace at type N points, none at types I, II, D and III. [[c:synthesis.attachment-transport-is-flat-only-where-weyl-vanishes]] No conformal-energy generator commutes with a nonzero Weyl curvature, so off Weyl-flat regions the attachment supplies no state. [[c:synthesis.attachment-transport-is-flat-only-where-weyl-vanishes]] Real black holes, which are never half-flat, lie outside its reach. [[c:correspondence.no-real-lorentzian-vacuum-half-flat]]

title: On a gravitational field the conformal spinors of the attachment are parallel for the tractor gauge field only where the Weyl curvature vanishes: at a type N point a two-dimensional subspace can be, at points of type I, II, D or III none, and no conformal-energy generator commutes with a nonzero Weyl curvature, so off Weyl-flat regions the tractor transport of the attachment supplies no state
text: The series links its quantum modes to spacetime through a special four-dimensional space of spinors, which in flat space comes with a built-in notion of positive energy. In a gravitational field one has to carry that space from point to point, and gravity's tidal part, the Weyl curvature, twists it on the way. This result shows that the space survives only where that tidal part vanishes: at a point of one special radiation type half of it can survive, and at every other point none of it, and the built-in notion of positive energy is lost. So in a general gravitational field this way of attaching the modes does not fix the quantum state; the state has to be supplied in some other way.

title: Results cited, not shown
Imported: the theorems that deliver $2\pi$, and their hypotheses
text: These are the standard theorems of quantum field theory that produce the factor $2\pi$ behind the Unruh and Hawking temperatures. They say that when energy is positive and the theory respects relativity and locality, the natural internal clock of the region on one side of a horizon is the horizon's boost, running at a fixed rate. The entry records their hypotheses, since those are what any attempt to use them must supply.
provenance: J. J. Bisognano and E. H. Wichmann, On the duality condition for a Hermitian scalar field, J. Math. Phys. 16 (1975), 985--1007.; J. J. Bisognano and E. H. Wichmann, On the duality condition for quantum fields, J. Math. Phys. 17 (1976), 303--321.; H.-J. Borchers, The CPT-theorem in two-dimensional theories of local observables, Commun. Math. Phys. 143 (1992), 315--332.; P. D. Hislop and R. Longo, Modular structure of the local algebras associated with the free massless scalar field theory, Commun. Math. Phys. 84 (1982), 71--85.; R. Brunetti, D. Guido and R. Longo, Modular structure and duality in conformal quantum field theory, Commun. Math. Phys. 156 (1993), 201--219.; G. L. Sewell, Quantum fields on manifolds: PCT and gravitationally induced thermal states, Ann. Phys. 141 (1982), 201--224.; B. S. Kay and R. M. Wald, Theorems on the uniqueness and thermal properties of stationary, nonsingular, quasifree states on spacetimes with a bifurcate Killing horizon, Phys. Rep. 207 (1991), 49--136.; W. G. Unruh, Notes on black-hole evaporation, Phys. Rev. D 14 (1976), 870--892.

title: Imported: the tractor connection, and the conformal spinor connection (local twistor transport)
text: Gravity on flat spacetime determines a conformal geometry, which carries two standard ways of carrying data from point to point. One acts on the six-component vectors of the series' conformal model, called tractors, and on flat spacetime it is itself a gauge field built from gravity; the other acts on four-component spinors of the conformal geometry. This entry records both formulas, taken from the literature, in the conventions the series uses.
provenance: Transport Lab claim correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport, version 6 (T09 Fact 4.9)

title: Imported: Weyl commutes with duality
text: In four dimensions, the part of the gravitational field strength responsible for tidal forces and gravitational waves respects a natural symmetry that exchanges electric-type and magnetic-type components. This is a standard result of relativity, imported here.
provenance: R. Penrose and W. Rindler, Spinors and Space-Time, Vols. 1--2, Cambridge University Press (1984, 1986).

title: Imported: Weyl's theorem
text: In four or more dimensions, a gravitational field on flat spacetime amounts locally to nothing more than a change of scale exactly when one particular part of its strength, the Weyl curvature, is zero. This classical result is imported.
provenance: H. Weyl, Reine Infinitesimalgeometrie, Math. Z. 2 (1918), 384--411.

title: Lorentzian duality is a complex structure
text: In four-dimensional spacetime the Hodge star sends each plane element to a complementary one. Doing it twice gives minus the original, just as multiplying by the imaginary unit twice gives minus one. So once complex numbers are allowed, the plane elements split into two three-dimensional halves, self-dual and anti-self-dual, which are complex conjugates of each other.
provenance: Transport Lab claim correspondence.lorentzian-duality-complex-structure, version 3 (T09 Lem 6.4)

title: Imported: the frozen point and its geometry (external ingredients)
text: The frozen-point fact rests partly on mathematics from outside the series. This entry names that source: Gover's work on tractor bundles, which supplies the connection and the scale tractor that the fact uses.
provenance: A. R. Gover, Almost Einstein and Poincar'e-Einstein manifolds in Riemannian signature, J. Geom. Phys. 60 (2010), 182--204.

title: Second quantisation
text: Fields whose values are elements of the spacetime algebra and whose modes are tower planes can be quantised inside one algebra, with the volume element as imaginary unit. The resulting field is local, and its observables are the standard second-quantised ones. The price of this unit is that a field's two chiralities enter differently, one directly and one conjugated; Hestenes' unit avoids that at the cost of choosing a frame.
provenance: Transport Lab claim field-theory.second-quantisation, version 5 (FT Prop 5.2)

title: The attachment through conformal spinors
text: Since spacetime symmetries do not act on the tower's modes directly, the link must come from elsewhere. It comes from the series' conformal spinor storey, which provides positive-energy particle states with the right symmetry, while the Penrose transform turns them into waves in spacetime. On this reading the tower's levels are energy cut-offs rather than places, and the usual link between spin and statistics holds for the series' fermions.
provenance: Transport Lab claim field-theory.twistor-attachment, version 6 (FT Prop 3.2)

title: Where each imaginary unit lives
text: Every square root of minus one the field theory needs is an element of the real geometric algebra. The conformal spinors' unit is the conformal volume element, which on the spinors at a point becomes the spacetime volume element with a sign set by chirality. For massless fields the unit is the spacetime volume element, which agrees with Hestenes' choice up to that sign, while a mass term does not commute with it.
provenance: Transport Lab claim field-theory.where-each-lives, version 3 (FT Prop 4.1)

title: The I-state on the continuum
text: The earlier result about the horizon's equilibrium state was proved for a countable list of modes. This result carries it over to a continuous range of frequencies, as real radiation needs. The same thermal state, at the Hawking temperature, is again the only equilibrium state, and the energies need not be positive for this to hold.
provenance: Transport Lab claim hawking.i-state-continuum, version 5 (T07 Thm 4.2)

title: Imported: ideal-Fermi-gas uniqueness
text: For a gas of non-interacting fermions with a given energy rule, there is exactly one equilibrium state at each temperature, and its occupation numbers follow the Fermi-Dirac law. This is a textbook result of quantum statistical mechanics.
provenance: O. Bratteli and D. W. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 2, 2nd ed., Springer, Berlin (1997)., Ex.~5.3.2 and \S 5.3; H. Araki, On quasifree states of CAR and Bogoliubov automorphisms, Publ. RIMS Kyoto Univ. 6 (1971), 385--442.

title: Imported: quasi-free KMS reduces to the two-point level
text: For free fermions in the simplest class of states, checking thermal equilibrium needs only the two-particle correlations, because all higher correlations are built from them. This is a standard result of quantum statistical mechanics.
provenance: H. Araki, On quasifree states of CAR and Bogoliubov automorphisms, Publ. RIMS Kyoto Univ. 6 (1971), 385--442.; O. Bratteli and D. W. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 2, 2nd ed., Springer, Berlin (1997)., \S 5.3

title: Exact scale decoupling
text: Near a Schwarzschild black hole the tidal curvature has a fixed pattern: stretching in one pair of directions and squeezing in the others, in a two-to-one ratio. This result shows the pattern is exactly the same at every radius, all the way in towards the singularity. Only its overall strength, which grows like the inverse cube of the radius, changes.
provenance: Transport Lab claim interior.exact-scale-decoupling, version 4 (T06 Prop 3.3)

title: Imported: the Kerr curvature
text: This is the standard description of the strength of the gravitational field around a rotating black hole, the quantity that plays the part of spacetime curvature, written in the language of geometric algebra on a flat background. The strength of the curvature is controlled by a single complex number built from the radius and the angle from the rotation axis. The result is taken from the literature.
provenance: C. Doran and A. Lasenby, Geometric Algebra for Physicists, Cambridge University Press (2003)., Ch.~14; B. Carter, Global structure of the Kerr family of gravitational fields, Phys. Rev. 174 (1968), 1559--1571.

title: Imported: the tractor connection
text: Gravity here is a pair of fields on flat spacetime, and what it determines, once lengths are allowed to be rescaled freely, is a conformal geometry. To it one can attach a larger bundle called the tractor bundle, whose fibres are the six-dimensional vectors of the series' conformal model, with a natural way of differentiating its sections. This imported result gives that derivative explicitly once a particular scale is chosen, in terms of the Schouten tensor, a rearranged form of the field strength. The derivative depends only on the conformal geometry and respects the bundle's own metric.
provenance: T. N. Bailey, M. G. Eastwood and A. R. Gover, Thomas's structure bundle for conformal, projective and related structures, Rocky Mountain J. Math. 24 (1994), 1191--1217.; S. N. Curry and A. R. Gover, An introduction to conformal geometry and tractor calculus, with a view towards analysis on manifolds, in Asymptotic Analysis in General Relativity, London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series 443, Cambridge University Press (2018), 86--170., \S 5

title: The chart form of the spin isomorphism
text: The conformal symmetries of spacetime can be written either as rotations of a six-dimensional space or as four-by-four matrices acting on the four-component spinors of the conformal algebra. This lemma writes that translation out explicitly in the chart used for spacetime points. Dilations become a diagonal matrix, translations an upper corner block, and special conformal transformations a lower corner block.
provenance: Transport Lab claim mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism, version 5 (T11 Lem 5.3)

title: The Euclidean section, and its period
text: Replacing time by an imaginary variable turns the gravitational field outside a black hole into a field on a flat four-dimensional space without time, in which the time direction closes into a circle. Near the horizon the geometry this field describes looks like a flat plane in polar coordinates, but only if the circle has exactly the right length, $8\pi$ times the mass in natural units; any other length leaves a cone point. So the period is fixed by the gravitational field rather than chosen.
provenance: Transport Lab claim singularity.euclidean-section-period, version 5 (T05 Prop 7.18)

title: The chain
text: This result tests whether the three force strengths of the Standard Model can meet at a single high energy when the symmetry first enlarges to the Pati-Salam group at an intermediate scale. Assuming the slots of the composite's basic spinor states behave like the pairs (Hypothesis (S)), and with the particle content the framework then supplies, left-right symmetry broken only at the unification scale and nothing else light, they do meet, with the intermediate scale roughly between $10^{10}$ and $10^{12}$ GeV and the unification scale near $10^{16}$ GeV. At two loops, from the measured couplings' central values, the most favourable version passes the proton-decay limit comfortably, while a version that keeps left-right symmetry down to the intermediate scale does not.
provenance: Transport Lab claim standard-model.chain, version 8 (T12 Prop 10.10)

title: The connection is forced
text: Suppose matter fields carry both the spinor structure of the conformal algebra and the two-by-three internal structure, and that moving them from point to point must respect both. Then the only freedom left is a connection of a very particular kind, whose internal part takes values in exactly the Lie algebra of the Standard Model's forces. Under these assumptions the gauge fields are what the preserved structure allows, rather than an extra ingredient.
provenance: Transport Lab claim standard-model.connection-forced, version 4 (T12 Prop 5.7)

title: The twistor form on the conformal spinor space is the grading of the central rotation $Z = e_{0}\nu$ against the Hilbert form of the ladder-pair module, so the twistor attachment's conformal energy $|s| + 1 + n$ is the nonnegative generator of $Z$; every future translation, null special conformal transformation and de Sitter horizon generator is nonnegative on its modules, and the attachment's Fock vacuum satisfies the positivity and invariance clause of (N$_{+}$) on the local horizons of Minkowski space (and of de Sitter space for conformally invariant fields); on those horizons (N$_{+}$) is the choice of that vacuum as the state of the light rays, a restatement of the premise and not a derivation of it
text: The series needs the quantum fields near a horizon to carry no negative energy along its light rays. An earlier result showed this follows if the fields have nonnegative energy for one special symmetry, a rotation that mixes time with an extra direction of the series' enlarged algebra. Whether the series' own fields have that property had been left open. They do. The twistors from which the series builds its fields carry a quantity that can be positive or negative, and that special rotation is exactly what converts it into an ordinary positive length. Quantised, the rotation's energy comes out as the energies already stored for the fields, all positive, and every push along a light ray costs nonnegative energy too. So the vacuum of the series' fields satisfies the no-negative-energy condition on horizons in empty space, and on the horizon of an expanding universe for the fields that ignore rescaling, without assuming any temperature. That the fields are actually in that vacuum is still an assumption: the condition becomes the choice of this one state. Black holes are still not covered.
provenance: Transport Lab claim synthesis.attachment-conformal-energy-is-generated-by-z, version 1

title: On the attachment's helicity modules, the $L^{2}$ coefficient of the zero-point energy regulated by a smooth cut-off $L$ on conformal energy is $-(N_{V} - N_{W}/4)$ times one moment of the cut-off, reproducing the standard Sakharov weights; with $N_{V} = 12$, sixteen Weyl fields (right-handed neutrino included) in each of $N_{g}$ separate generations and conformally coupled scalars it vanishes exactly at $N_{g} = 3$, and a sharp cut-off at a floor adds terms that are not local
text: Sakharov suggested that gravity's strength might not be fundamental but induced by the quantum jitter of all the matter and force fields, the way a medium's stiffness comes from its atoms. This result tries that idea with the series' own particle states and a natural cut-off, the series' levels read as an energy limit. That cut-off only makes sense where the gravitational field has no tidal (Weyl) part, and it singles out one frame. Each kind of particle adds to the induced strength of gravity in proportion to the square of its spin, with force carriers and matter particles pulling in opposite directions. These weights are the standard ones, and the series' states reproduce them. With twelve force carriers and three separate families of sixteen matter states each, right-handed neutrinos included, the two cancel exactly. This is the standard count for the Standard Model with right-handed neutrinos, noticed in another form by Boyle and Turok. So under this cut-off the series' matter would induce no gravitational strength at leading order, if the leading term is read as gravity's, which is argued rather than proved. A sharp cut-off at the levels would also produce terms that no local law of gravity contains.

title: For a hole formed by collapse, with the outgoing sector reduced to one chiral CAR field per light ray (J3), the ground-state condition of (N$_{+}$) posed in its short-distance form on the ingoing sheet through each point of the future horizon, whose generator has both halves, gives the late-time state of the near-horizon exterior outgoing modes as the continuum I-state at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$: in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand gauge the Kruskal function $U = -e^{-\kappa t}(s-1)e^{s^{2}/2+s}$ is a regular parameter on that generator, dilated at rate $\kappa$ by the symmetry, so the late-time limit is exactly the scaling limit, which is the ground state for every kernel of the form ground-state singularity plus a remainder bounded near the horizon point, a class the same in every regular parameter for the weight-$\tfrac12$ kernel (sufficient condition; the null-shell realisation and the forcing of the temperature are a companion result)
text: A black hole that forms from a collapsing star has no past horizon, so the series' rule for the temperature of an eternal black hole, which looks at both sides of a horizon's light rays, cannot be applied as it stands. This result finds the rule that does apply. Through every point of the horizon there is a second family of light rays, the ones falling in; those cross the horizon from outside to inside and so always have two halves. The radiation that escapes to infinity is carried by the field's values along those infalling rays, measured in a coordinate that the hole's own time flow squeezes towards the horizon. Waiting a long time is the same as looking at ever shorter distances from the horizon, and at short distances any field that is not singular at the horizon looks like its own vacuum. Cutting that vacuum at the horizon, by a result already in the series, gives a thermal state at Hawking's temperature. So the condition for a collapsing hole is the series' existing vacuum condition, applied to the infalling rays and only at short distances; it is enough for the thermal outcome, though not the only condition that gives it. One state that fails it is the one that would make the horizon a place of infinite energy. The result treats each light ray's field as a one-dimensional field, an assumption the series states separately.

title: The cosmological horizon's boost is the frozen point's time translation
text: In the series the cosmological constant is carried by one fixed vector of the enlarged algebra, the frozen point. This result shows that the time flow seen by an observer in a universe with a positive cosmological constant is a single boost built from that vector, and that the boost's rate, which fixes how strongly the observer's horizon pulls, is exactly the square root of the frozen point's squared length. With no cosmological constant the same construction gives ordinary time translation and no horizon; with a negative one it gives a rotation, and time closes on itself.

title: The standard null-cone form of the Einstein condition, translated into vacuum language: infinity vacua unexcited along their own light rays
text: A known way of stating Einstein's condition on empty space is that the curvature felt along every light ray has no part of a certain kind. This result translates that known statement into the series' language of quantum vacua; it does not derive it. In the series, every point of spacetime carries a small family of quantum vacuum states, and so does the point at infinity that a choice of scale singles out. Each such vacuum is attached to one light-ray direction. The vacua of an ordinary point are never disturbed when you move along their own light ray, in any spacetime: that is pure geometry. This result shows that asking the same of the vacua at infinity, that moving along their own light ray never disturbs them, is exactly Einstein's condition on the curvature, with the cosmological constant left free. Asking that they are never disturbed in any direction gives empty space with no cosmological constant, and asking it of one vacuum only gives a beam of pure radiation. With matter present, the disturbance along each light ray equals the matter's energy flowing along it exactly when Einstein's equations hold, the cosmological constant appearing as a free constant. These are equivalences: the result translates Einstein's condition into the language of vacua and does not explain why nature would impose it.

title: The Euler part of the series' horizon entropy on a patch of a cut is an edge term, $\alpha$ times the holonomy angle of the cut's own rotation-gauge field around the patch edge; with the edge's geodesic-curvature term (the two-dimensional Gibbons-Hawking term, a choice within the edge ambiguity of the Noether charge, argued not derived) it becomes the constant $2\pi\alpha\chi(P) = -3\pi\chi(P)/2\Lambda$, so with that edge term the Wald reading of the series' action and the Clausius route agree on every entropy change of an open patch and differ by a topological constant that no additive edge term built from the field and the cut removes, and which for $\Lambda > 0$ makes the entropy negative on every disk patch of area below $6\pi/\Lambda$
text: The series' gravitational action contains an extra term (the Euler term) which leaves Einstein's equations unchanged but, in the standard recipe, adds a curvature-dependent piece to the entropy of a horizon. A stored result showed that this piece changes along small patches of a horizon with no heat flowing, which clashes with the heat-balance route to Einstein's equations. This result shows that the troublesome piece of a patch is really a property of the patch's edge: it equals a fixed multiple of the angle by which a direction carried around the edge within the patch's own surface turns. Adding the standard edge correction (how sharply the edge bends), which is a natural choice rather than one forced by the action, turns the piece into a fixed number set only by the patch's shape type, the same for every disk-shaped patch. Then the entropy changes exactly as the heat-balance route requires. What is left is a constant that no edge correction can remove; it is the same constant already known for closed horizons, and it is removed by the existing normalisation, not by anything in the series' objects. Without that normalisation the constant would even make the entropy of small patches negative.

title: The tractor connection as a rotation-gauge field of the conformal model on flat spacetime

These equations are standard textbook geometry; the series uses them in the step where the energy flowing through a small horizon is converted into the strength of the gravitational field.
provenance: A. Raychaudhuri, Relativistic cosmology. I, Phys. Rev. 98 (1955), 1123--1126.; R. K. Sachs, Gravitational waves in general relativity. VI. The outgoing radiation condition, Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 264 (1961), 309--338.; R. M. Wald, General Relativity, University of Chicago Press (1984).

In the simplest version each kind of field contributes a fixed weight, and force-carrying fields count four times as strongly, with the opposite sign, as matter fields. With the known particles plus right-handed neutrinos, the matter fields number exactly four times the force carriers, a coincidence noticed in another context by Boyle and Turok. These are taken from the literature.

title: On the integrated reading of (Loc), the Clausius relation with the de Sitter calibration forces a continuous entropy density to 1/4 on every admissible field whose local data approach calibrated data; so a continuous density depending on curvature alone that keeps the flat Friedmann fields with $w \in [0,1]$ and $\Lambda \ge 0$ admissible is 1/4 at every curvature they pass through, the Einstein static universe's among them; a density that depends on matter as well escapes with every field satisfying Einstein's equations at the calibrated coupling admissible
text: To get Einstein's equations from heat flow across horizons, one assumes that every small piece of horizon carries the same entropy per unit area. Earlier work showed that the heat-flow law already forces this entropy to be the same throughout any one universe, but possibly different in different universes. This result asks when that loophole can actually be used. If the entropy depends smoothly on how strongly space is curved, the loophole closes for any universe that thins out toward empty space, and expanding universes of ordinary matter pass through every isotropic curvature on their way, including that of Einstein's static universe, the old example of an escape. If the entropy may also depend on the matter itself, the loophole stays open: an explicit rule gives the standard value in every ordinary universe and a different value, with a weaker gravity, in Einstein's static universe.

title: Under the Gupta-Bleuler form of the Krein premise, the Krein quartet of a covariantly gauge-fixed vector drops level by level from the induced Einstein-Hilbert coefficient under an energy cut-off on the Einstein static field, but under a heat-kernel cut-off on the gauge-fixed operators the vector's weight is $\alpha - 5$, equal to the two-helicity value $-4$ only at the Gupta-Bleuler value $\alpha = 1$; so under that cut-off the series' content induces $12(\alpha - 1) + 8(1 - 6\xi_{R})$ minimal-scalar units, fixed by the content only together with the regulator and the gauge
text: Sakharov's idea is that the strength of gravity could be induced by the quantum jitter of all the other fields. Each kind of field adds or subtracts a definite amount, and an earlier result showed that the series' force carriers and matter particles cancel exactly, at least for one way of cutting off the jitter at short distances. Force carriers come with extra bookkeeping modes that describe nothing physical and are removed in the end. This result checks, under the series' premise for these modes (an indefinite inner product), whether they really drop out of the count. With a cut-off on energy they do, level by level. With a cut-off that treats space and time alike, they do only for one particular choice of the bookkeeping, and otherwise each force carrier shifts the count. So the cancellation depends on the cut-off and the bookkeeping, not only on which particles exist. The series' own choice of bookkeeping is the one that keeps the cancellation, provided the Higgs fields couple to curvature in the special conformal way.
